To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the sentiment expressed by a user in a discussion is an informative signal for the presence or absence of a dispute, (2) a simple approach to sentiment tagging of sentences in a discussion is sufficient to achieve good results, (3) the best model is a simple classifier that combines features from sentiment tagging with features from other sources, and (4) our approach to dispute detection is robust to the presence of noise and can be used to automatically flag discussions that require human attention.

(i) we propose a sentiment analysis approach for online dispute detection, (ii) we evaluate it on a newly created dataset and find that it outperforms other approaches, and (iii) we find that our approach is robust to the presence of noise.

we have created a dataset for dispute detection, that we have developed an approach for sentiment analysis that works well in the domain of Wikipedia discussions and that we have shown that the combination of our sentiment analysis and a classifier that uses the sentiment tags as input features leads to the best performing model.
